config.title: Feature Flag Hook

intro.title: Feature Flag Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useFeatureFlag` that allows you to conditionally enable or disable features in your application. You'll learn how to create a reusable hook that manages a boolean state to control feature visibility. The main technologies involved are React hooks like `useState` and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a practical hook you can integrate into components to toggle UI elements based on feature flags.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are used in production applications to control feature visibility without redeploying code. For example, e-commerce platforms use them to gradually roll out new checkout flows to specific user segments. SaaS dashboards employ feature flags to enable premium features for paying customers while hiding them from free users. This pattern allows developers to test features in production, perform A/B testing, and quickly disable problematic features if issues arise.

objectives: Construct a custom React hook that manages feature flag state
Initialize the hook with a configuration object containing flag names and default values
Implement a toggle function within the hook to change feature flag states
Apply the custom hook within a React component to conditionally render UI elements
Bind feature flag states to component logic that controls user interface behavior
Configure a component to update its display based on changes to feature flags
Integrate the feature flag hook with multiple components in a small application

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for building a custom hook are added to the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the useFeatureFlag hook interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named FeatureFlagReturn that specifies two properties: isEnabled (boolean) and toggle (a function that returns void).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the FeatureFlagReturn interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named FeatureFlagReturn is defined with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagReturn interface has isEnabled: boolean and toggle: () => void properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that both properties (isEnabled and toggle) are defined with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface isn't quite right. Make sure you're using the 'interface' keyword, the correct name, and both required properties.

steps.title: Define the useFeatureFlag hook function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'useFeatureFlag' that takes an initial boolean parameter and returns the FeatureFlagReturn interface.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts a boolean parameter and returns an object matching the FeatureFlagReturn interface you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A useFeatureFlag function is defined with proper TypeScript typing that accepts a boolean parameter and returns the FeatureFlagReturn interface.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag function is defined with a boolean parameter and returns an object matching the FeatureFlagReturn interface.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts a boolean parameter and returns an object matching the FeatureFlagReturn interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match the requirements. It should be named 'useFeatureFlag', accept a boolean parameter, and return the FeatureFlagReturn interface.

steps.title: Add state to track feature flag status
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag hook function, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'isEnabled' that tracks the feature flag status, initialized with the 'initialValue' parameter.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initialValue parameter to create the state variable and its setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: useState for a toggle state
const [isOn, setIsOn] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook will have a state variable 'isEnabled' initialized with the provided initialValue parameter.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with initialValue, and the state variable is named 'isEnabled'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the useState hook with the initialValue parameter and naming the state variable 'isEnabled'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state variable wasn't properly set up. Remember to use useState with the initialValue parameter inside the hook function.

steps.title: Create the toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag hook, define a function named toggleFlag that toggles the isEnabled state using the setter from useState.
steps.hint: Use the setter function from useState to update the state to the opposite of its current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleFlag function is defined inside the hook, ready to be returned as part of the hook's return value.
successCriteria: A toggleFlag function is defined that calls setIsEnabled with the opposite of the current isEnabled value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly toggles the isEnabled state using the setter from useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler function is missing or incorrect. Define a function named toggleFlag that toggles the isEnabled state.

steps.title: Return the hook's interface values
steps.instruction: Complete the useFeatureFlag hook by returning an object with isEnabled set to the state variable and toggleFlag set to the toggle handler function.
steps.hint: The return statement should match the FeatureFlagReturn interface you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook should return an object with isEnabled and toggleFlag properties that match the FeatureFlagReturn interface.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag hook returns an object containing isEnabled and toggleFlag properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with both isEnabled and toggleFlag properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't returning the expected values. Check that you're returning an object matching the FeatureFlagReturn interface.

steps.title: Create the FeatureFlagDemo component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named FeatureFlagDemo that will use the useFeatureFlag hook. The component should return a JSX wrapper element (like a div).
steps.hint: Define a function called FeatureFlagDemo that returns a div element. You'll add content inside it in later steps.
steps.expectedOutcome: A FeatureFlagDemo component is defined and returns a div wrapper.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagDemo component is created as a function that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the component, but make sure it's a function named FeatureFlagDemo that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function called FeatureFlagDemo that returns a div.

steps.title: Use the hook in the demo component
steps.instruction: Inside the FeatureFlagDemo component, call the useFeatureFlag hook with an initial value of false and destructure the returned isEnabled and toggleFlag values.
steps.hint: Call the hook at the top of the component and destructure the returned object into two variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeatureFlagDemo component now has access to the feature flag state and toggle function through the custom hook.
successCriteria: useFeatureFlag is called with false as the initial value
isEnabled and toggleFlag are destructured from the hook return value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useFeatureFlag with false and destructuring both isEnabled and toggleFlag.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook hasn't been properly integrated. Remember to call useFeatureFlag with false and destructure the returned values.

steps.title: Add UI to display feature flag status
steps.instruction: Inside the FeatureFlagDemo component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current feature flag status. The text should show 'Feature is enabled: ' followed by the isEnabled value.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to render a

tag. Inside the tag, you can display text and the isEnabled value using curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph that displays the current feature flag status (true or false).
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside the component's return statement that displays 'Feature is enabled: ' followed by the isEnabled value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're displaying the isEnabled value in the paragraph, not just static text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the isEnabled value correctly.

steps.title: Add toggle button with click handler
steps.instruction: In the FeatureFlagDemo component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Toggle Feature Flag' and wire its onClick event to the toggleFlag function from the hook.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the <div>. Use onClick={toggleFlag} to connect it to the toggle handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will include a button that, when clicked, toggles the feature flag status between enabled and disabled.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Toggle Feature Flag' exists and its onClick handler is correctly wired to the toggleFlag function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and onClick handler wired to toggleFlag.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected. Check that you added a <button> with onClick={toggleFlag}.
